findings.statement: Approval binding, invalidation, and completion blocking are demonstrated as Runtime V2 contract fixtures, while executor-side one-shot consumption and dispatch authority remain intentionally unimplemented.
findings.defect_hypothesis: A future executor could treat recorded approval state as sufficient authority without consuming the bound record at dispatch.
findings.impact: The current evidence supports only a qualified contract observation, not enforcement of an executed action.
findings.safety_red_line: No dispatch or terminal success may be inferred from a durable approval record alone.
findings.limitation: There is no executor implementation or separately authorized action to exercise in P4.

findings.statement: The public P3 receipt reports suite-level totals, while future aggregation must reject duplicate case identifiers before a per-case map and raw-list totals can diverge.
findings.defect_hypothesis: A duplicated case ID in a future trial receipt could yield inconsistent aggregate counts and distort a P5 denominator.
findings.impact: The P3 result is not contradicted, but P5 metric integrity needs an explicit duplicate-ID rejection check before scoring.
findings.safety_red_line: Do not aggregate a trial set with duplicate case identifiers.
findings.limitation: This is a prospective scoring-control finding, not evidence of a P3 grading error.
